title: Prefatio: preach free election; Pontifical reduction of the mystery
pass_a_gloss: If we press Paul's footsteps, if we imitate the example of holy Augustine, if we cling to the doctrine received in this our Church, there is no danger of scandal. On the contrary, if we suffer the doctrine of free election to be overwhelmed and buried, or (what is baser) if we bear with equal mind that doctrine corrupted worst by certain Pontificals and others and twisted into the contrary, this inert silence will certainly not lack suspicion: for a ready defense of truth would meet us, if promulgated falsehood were displeasing. I think it is hidden from none of you that many from the Pontifical writers have recalled this whole mystery of election and reprobation, at which Paul stood astonished, to an all-too-clear and easy account of the difference, while they philosophize that some are elected from foreknowledge of merits, but others rejected from foreknowledge of demerits.
pass_b_english: If we follow Paul's steps, imitate holy Augustine, and hold the doctrine received in this our Church, there is no danger of scandal. But if we let the doctrine of free election be overwhelmed and buried — or, worse, if we calmly endure it when certain Papal writers and others have badly corrupted it and twisted it the other way — that lazy silence will not escape suspicion. A ready defense of the truth would meet us if published falsehood displeased us. None of you, I think, fails to see that many Papal writers have reduced this whole mystery of election and reprobation — at which Paul stood astonished — to an all-too-clear and easy account of the difference, teaching that some are chosen from foreknowledge of merits, others rejected from foreknowledge of demerits.
source_text: Si Pauli vestigia premamus, si sancti Augustini exemplum imitemur, si doctrinae in hac Ecclesia nostra receptae adhaerescamus, nullum scandali periculum est. E contra, si obrui & sepeliri patiamur doctrinam gratuita electionis, aut (quod turpius est) si illam a quibusdam Pontificiis aliisque pessime corruptam & in contrarium detortam aequo animo feramus, non carebit utique suspicione haec iners taciturnitas: occurreret enim nobis expedita defensio veritatis, si falsitas promulgata displiceret. Neminem vestrum latere arbitror, ex Pontificiis scriptoribus multos, totum hoc mysterium electionis & reprobationis, in quo Paulus obstupuit, ad nimis claram facilemque discriminis rationem revocasse, dum alios ex praescientia meritorum electos, alios autem ex praescientia demeritorum rejectos philosophorum.
